result:
Post revisions are implemented; `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` passes (12 tests, 10 of them new), and lint, `guren check` and `guren audit` report no failures.

One decision you may want to revisit: I reused the existing `update` policy for both revision routes rather than adding a separate ability, so whoever may edit a post may see and restore its history.

**Summary of changes.** I added a `post_revisions` table (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at` as ISO text, foreign key to `posts` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`) in `db/schema.ts`, with the generated migration in `db/migrations/20260929185245_add_post_revisions_table/`. A new `app/Models/PostRevision.ts` model backs it, and `app/Models/Post.ts` gained `Post.revise()` (snapshots the previous version and updates the post in one transaction) and `Post.deleteWithRevisions()` (deletes history and post together, explicitly rather than relying on the cascade). `PostController.update` and `PostController.destroy` in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts` now call these. The new `app/Http/Controllers/PostRevisionController.ts` serves `GET /posts/:id/revisions` (props `post` and `revisions: [{ id, title, excerpt, createdAt }]`, newest first) and `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` (redirects to `/posts/:id`, 404 when the revision belongs to another post). Both routes are registered in the `auth` group in `routes/web.ts` as `posts.revisions.index` and `posts.revisions.restore`, so guests go to `/login` and non-authors get 403. Supporting pieces are `app/Http/Resources/PostRevisionResource.ts`, a `PostRevisionParamSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts`, the new page `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx`, an author-only "Revisions" link in `resources/js/pages/posts/Show.tsx`, and regenerated `.guren/*.gen.ts` files via `bun run codegen`. Tests are in `tests/PostRevisionController.test.ts` and run against the test database.
